findings.evidence: grep 'SimplyConnected\|prodMulEquivOfSimplyConnected' TorusFundamentalGroup.lean → no hits; only importer of FundamentalGroupProduct is the torus file, which uses prodMulEquiv/piMulEquiv. Roadmap Stage 4 (UniversalCovers/README.md lines 139-145) lists π_n(S¹), π₁(S¹), π_n(Tᵏ), π₁(RPⁿ), K(G,1) — none a product with a simply connected factor. Author's own description: the cylinder application is 'on no proximate path to any named Stage 4 target.'
findings.fix: Point to a genuine Stage 4 consumer (RPⁿ, K(G,1), etc.) that proximately needs collapsing a simply connected factor, or have a human add product/simply-connected-factor collapse to the UniversalCovers roadmap before merging.
findings.issue: prodMulEquivOfSimplyConnectedRight/Left (and the enabling FundamentalGroup.instUnique) are new content with no proximate path to a named UniversalCovers Stage 4 target. The claimed path — the torus computation — is refuted: TorusFundamentalGroup.lean already computes π₁(Tᵏ) via prodMulEquiv over circle factors (none simply connected) and does not reference the collapse lemmas. The lemma's natural application, the cylinder S¹×ℝ, was removed by the author as off-roadmap; nothing else consumes it.

summary: The collapse-of-simply-connected-factor lemmas are new mathematical content whose stated path (the torus) is not real — the torus π₁ is already computed on main from prodMulEquiv over circle factors and neither uses nor needs collapsing a simply connected factor. No named Stage 4 target (Tᵏ, RPⁿ, K(G,1)) is a product with a simply connected factor, and the lemma's only concrete application (the cylinder S¹×ℝ) was itself removed as off-roadmap; the API has no consumer in the tree.
